title: Trends of world population
competency: Describe world and Ethiopian population growth and use doubling time to predict growth.

keywords.def: The total number of people living in an area at a given time.
A rapid, sudden increase of population.
The time a population needs to double itself. Doubling time = 70 ÷ growth rate.

ideas.name: How fast the world population grew

en.text: Human population is the number of people in an area at a given time. The world population has grown since the 15th century. It was about 791 million in 1750 and over 6 billion by 2000. Such rapid growth is called population explosion.

screens.title: 250 years of growth
screens.ask: In 1750 the world had about 791 million people. About how many were there by 2000?
screens.after: Over 6 billion. The population grew about 8 times in 250 years. This is called population explosion.

screens.title: 2.2 Trends of world population
paras: Human population is the total number of people in an area at a given time.
The area can be a city, a country or a continent.
Population shapes the social, economic and environmental life of every country.

screens.title: Population explosion
paras: The world population has grown since the 15th century.
The UNDP estimated 6 billion people by 2000, growing 1.5% a year.
At that rate, the population would double in 40–50 years.
Such rapid growth is called population explosion.

screens.title: Table 2.1 Trends in world population growth (millions)
screens.note: Source: Microsoft Encarta (2009). The 1950 and 2000 totals do not match the sum of the regions; see the notes.

screens.title: Factors of rapid population growth
paras: Advances in scientific knowledge, agriculture, industry and medicine.
Control of famine and disease, once major killers.
Cheaper vaccines, antibiotics, insecticides and high-yielding seeds.

screens.title: Key words
defs: The total number of people living in an area at a given time.
A rapid, sudden increase of population.

screens.text: Which region had the most people in 2000?
screens.why: Asia had 3,689 million in 2000, the largest number.
screens.clue: Look at the 2000 column of Table 2.1.

screens.text: Which is NOT a factor of rapid population growth?
screens.why: The book lists knowledge, medicine, better living and disease control. Illiteracy is not a cause of growth in the list.
screens.clue: Three options appear in the book's list.

screens.ask: From Table 2.1: Africa grew from 228 million in 1950 to 797 million in 2000. That is an increase of ___ million.
screens.clue: Subtract the 1950 number from the 2000 number.

screens.text: Using Table 2.1, which region's population is shown going DOWN between 2000 and 2050?
screens.why: Europe: 727 in 2000, 642 in 2050. (The table also shows Latin America falling; see the notes.)

screens.ask: From Table 2.1, North America grew from 221 million (1950) to 481 million (2000). How many times bigger is that, to one decimal place? ___ times
screens.why: 481 ÷ 221 = 2.176… ≈ 2.2. So North America became about 2.2 times bigger.
screens.clue: Divide the 2000 number by the 1950 number.

en.text: Doubling time is how long a population needs to double. Doubling time = 70 ÷ growth rate. At 1.5% a year it is about 47 years. Ethiopia had 11.8 million people in 1900 and 73.8 million in 2007. Its growth rate peaked at 3.1% in 1984 and fell to 2.0% in 2007.

screens.title: When will it double?
screens.ask: A town grows by 2% every year. About how long until its population doubles?

screens.title: Focus: doubling time
paras: Population doubling time is the time a population needs to double itself.
Example: at 1.5% a year, 70 ÷ 1.5 ≈ 46.7 years. This fits "40–50 years".

screens.title: Trend and growth rate of Ethiopian population
paras: The 2007 Census counted 73.8 million people in Ethiopia.
In 1900 Ethiopia had about 11.8 million people. By 1960 it had 23.5 million, twice as many.
So it took 60 years to double. Since 1960 the doubling time has become shorter.
The growth rate rose after the 1950s, when malaria and other diseases were controlled.
It fell from 3.1% in 1984 to 2.9% in 1994 and 2.0% in 2007, mainly because of family planning services.

screens.title: Table 2.2 Population and growth rate in Ethiopia
Key words
defs: The time a population needs to double itself. Doubling time = 70 ÷ growth rate.

screens.ask: A population grows at 2% a year. Doubling time = 70 ÷ 2 = ___ years.
Ethiopia's growth rate in 2007 was 2.0%. Its doubling time is ___ years.

screens.text: In which year was Ethiopia's growth rate highest (Table 2.2)?
screens.why: The table shows 3.1% in 1984, the highest value.
screens.clue: Find the biggest number in the growth-rate row.

screens.ask: At 3.5% a year, doubling time = ___ years.
A town has 10,000 people and doubles every 35 years. How many people after 70 years? ___
screens.why: After 35 years: 10,000 × 2 = 20,000. After another 35 years: 20,000 × 2 = 40,000. 70 years is two doubling times.
screens.clue: How many doubling times are in 70 years?

items.text: 1. Which two continents' population growth differs the most (Tables 2.1 and 2.2)?
items.why: From 2000 to 2050, Africa grows from 797 to 1,846 million, while Europe falls from 727 to 642 million.
items.clue: Compare the growth of each continent from 2000 to 2050.

items.text: 2. Which is a measure to correct rapid population growth?
items.why: Ethiopia's growth rate fell mainly because of family planning services.

items.text: 3. How did Ethiopia's population grow from 1900 to 2007?
opts: Slowly at first, then very fast; the rate fell after 1984
items.ans: Slowly at first, then very fast; the rate fell after 1984
items.why: It took 60 years to double (1900–1960), then grew fast to 73.8 million by 2007.
